hints: Look closely at the functional groups in tartaric acid and think about which ones are acidic enough to react with dilute NaOH.
Remember that excess LiAlH4 reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols, so work out the structure of J as HOCH2CH(OH)CH(OH)CH2OH.
Compare a carboxylic acid with an alcohol toward NaOH(aq) to decide which starting material and which product will actually be neutralised.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional groups in tartaric acid**

Tartaric acid is $\text{HOOCCH(OH)CH(OH)COOH}$. It has two carboxylic acid groups ($\text{-COOH}$) and two alcohol groups ($\text{-OH}$).

Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to react with NaOH(aq).

**Find product J from LiAlH4 reduction**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent. It reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols:
$$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{excess LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$
So both $\text{-COOH}$ groups become $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups. Product J is:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
J is a tetra-ol with four alcohol groups and no acid groups.

**Test each compound with NaOH(aq)**

Tartaric acid reacts by neutralisation to form a salt and water:
$$\text{RCOOH + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa + H}_2\text{O}$$
Alcohols like J are very weak acids and do not react with aqueous NaOH. They need reactive sodium metal to react, not NaOH.

Therefore only tartaric acid reacts.

options.A: Incorrect. This assumes the alcohol groups in J also react with NaOH(aq). Alcohols are far too weakly acidic to be deprotonated by dilute NaOH, so J shows no reaction.
options.B: Correct. Tartaric acid contains -COOH groups which are neutralised by NaOH to give sodium tartrate and water. J is HOCH2CH(OH)CH(OH)CH2OH, a polyol with only -OH groups, which do not react with NaOH(aq).
options.C: Incorrect and reversed. It is the carboxylic acid that reacts with base, not the alcohol product. J has lost both -COOH groups by reduction, so it cannot be neutralised.
options.D: Incorrect. This ignores normal acid-base chemistry. Carboxylic acids definitely react with NaOH(aq), so tartaric acid must react even though J does not.
